mainTopic: The failed attempts at a conditional פסח, the father's race to ירושלים, and the deadlines for joining or leaving a פסח
overview: This amud opens in the middle of a discussion about five people who each brought a פסח, where one animal turned out to have a מום and nobody knows whose it was. The גמרא tries again and again to let them bring a new animal with a condition: if I still owe a פסח, it is a פסח; if not, it is a שלמים or a מותר הפסח. Each time, the גמרא finds a difference between the two offerings that blocks the condition: the חזה ושוק, the eating time, סמיכה, the number of blood placements, and pouring versus throwing the blood. The final answer is that pouring שלמים blood is valid only בדיעבד, never as a plan לכתחילה, so the condition cannot work. Next comes a משנה about a father who slaughters a פסח for whichever son reaches ירושלים first. The גמרא asks if this proves ברירה. רבי יוחנן answers that all the children were registered from the start, and the race was only to make them eager for מצוות. A precise reading of the משנה and a ברייתא support him. Last, a new משנה teaches that people may join a פסח as long as each gets a כזית, and may register or withdraw until the שחיטה. אביי explains that רבי שמעון extends only the time for withdrawing, until the blood is thrown, and a ברייתא confirms this.

steps.title: The breast and thigh problem blocks the conditional offering
steps.stepSummary: A conditional פסח-or-שלמים offering fails because the חזה ושוק belong to כהנים only if it is שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because there is the breast and the thigh, which are eaten by the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the five people cannot simply bring a new animal on condition that it is either a פסח or a שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שלמים has a חזה ושוק that must be given to the כהנים. A פסח has no such gift; its owners eat all of it. Under the condition we never know which one it is, so we cannot know who is allowed to eat the breast and thigh.

keyTerms.meaning: The breast and the thigh, parts of a שלמים given to the כהנים
Priests
Peace offering
The Paschal offering

phrases.english: Because there is the breast and the thigh,
phrases.notes: This answers the previous question of why a conditional offering does not work.

phrases.english: which the priests are the ones who eat it.
phrases.notes: This applies only if the animal is שלמים, not if it is a פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question on the previous amud: why not bring a conditional פסח or שלמים?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The condition fails because the rules for who eats the חזה ושוק differ between פסח and שלמים.

steps.title: Suggestion that each person register a priest
steps.stepSummary: Each person could register a כהן on his animal, so a כהן eats the חזה ושוק either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let each and every one bring a כהן along with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back with a fix: have a כהן registered on each animal. This sets up the next step, which tests whether the fix works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a כהן is one of the registered eaters, he can eat the חזה ושוק in any case. If it is a פסח, he eats it as a member of the group; if it is שלמים, he eats it as a כהן. This seems to remove the problem from Step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him bring (a suggestion)
Each and every one
With him

phrases.aramaic: וְנַיְתֵי כׇּל חַד וְחַד כֹּהֵן בַּהֲדֵיהּ.
phrases.english: Then let each and every one bring a priest with him.
phrases.notes: The priest would be registered on that person's new animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנַיְתֵי כׇּל חַד וְחַד כֹּהֵן בַּהֲדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 1 by offering a way around the חזה ושוק problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 1 that the חזה ושוק makes the condition unworkable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A registered כהן is allowed to eat the חזה ושוק whether the animal is פסח or שלמים, so the doubt no longer matters.

steps.title: Any single priest has a problem either way
steps.stepSummary: A כהן who already brought a פסח cannot register; a כהן who did not may lose his own פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of כהן is this? If he already brought a פסח, perhaps this animal is a פסח, and it turns out a פסח is eaten by someone not validly registered. If he did not bring a פסח, perhaps this animal is a שלמים, and he ends up never bringing a פסח!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the fix from Step 2 by asking which kind of כהן we would use. Both options cause a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option 1: a כהן who already brought a פסח cannot validly register for another one, so if this animal is really a פסח, it is eaten by someone not truly on it. Option 2: a כהן who still owes a פסח is relying on this animal, but if it turns out to be שלמים, he has missed his מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? What case is this?
Perhaps
By those not registered for it
Performed / brought the פסח

steps.confusionAlert: The כהן here is not a problem because he is a כהן. He is a problem because he is also a person registering to eat a פסח, so the question is whether he still owes his own פסח.

phrases.english: This priest, what is his case?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is about to check both possibilities, one at a time.

phrases.english: If he already performed the Pesach,
phrases.notes: This is the first possibility.

phrases.english: perhaps this animal is a Pesach,
and it turns out a Pesach is eaten by those not registered for it.
phrases.notes: Someone who already brought a פסח cannot validly register for another.

phrases.english: And if he did not perform the Pesach,
phrases.notes: This is the second possibility.

phrases.aramaic: דִּילְמָא שְׁלָמִים הוּא, וְלָא עָבֵיד פֶּסַח!
phrases.english: perhaps it is a peace offering, and he will not have performed the Pesach!
phrases.notes: He would lose his own מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion of Step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole idea of attaching one כהן to each individual animal
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Every kind of כהן fails: one who already brought a פסח cannot validly register, and one who has not brought a פסח might miss his own obligation.

steps.title: One priest registered on all five animals
steps.stepSummary: All five register one כהן who has not brought a פסח. One of the five animals must be a real פסח, so he fulfills his obligation either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let all five bring one כהן who has not brought a פסח, and let him register on all five of these offerings. Whichever way you look at it, there is one person who has not brought a פסח, and the כהן fulfills his obligation with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא improves the fix: instead of a separate כהן for each animal, all five share one כהן who still owes a פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fixes the second problem in Step 3. We know one of the five truly has not fulfilled the מצוה, so one of the five new animals is surely a real פסח. The כהן is registered on all five, so he is sure to fulfill his own פסח through that one, and he may eat the חזה ושוק of the others.

keyTerms.meaning: All five together
And let him register on it
Whichever way you look at it
He fulfills his obligation with it

steps.whatToRemember: The final suggestion uses מִמָּה נַפְשָׁךְ logic. One of the five animals is surely a real פסח, so one shared כהן who still owes a פסח is guaranteed to fulfill his מצוה, and he solves the חזה ושוק problem.

phrases.english: Then let all five bring one priest
phrases.notes: One shared כהן instead of five.

phrases.english: who has not performed the Pesach,
and let him register on these five Pesach offerings,
since whichever way you look at it, there is one
phrases.notes: One of the five surely still owes a פסח.

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא עָבֵיד פֶּסַח, וְקָא נָפְקִי בֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: who has not performed the Pesach, and he fulfills his obligation with him.
phrases.notes: That person's new animal is a real פסח, and the כהן is registered on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנַיְתֵי כֹּל חַמְשָׁה חַד כֹּהֵן דְּלָא עֲבַד פֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Revises the rejected suggestion of Step 2 to avoid the problem raised in Step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion from Steps 1 and 3 that no workable conditional solution exists
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One shared כהן who still owes a פסח is certain to fulfill his מצוה through whichever of the five animals is the true פסח, so the dilemma of Step 3 disappears.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא uses a shared doubt among a group to create certainty for one person, a common method in cases of mixed-up offerings.

steps.title: The condition fails because it shortens the eating time of שלמים
steps.stepSummary: After the כהן problem was solved, the גמרא gives a new reason the condition cannot work: a פסח may be eaten for only one day and one night, while שלמים may be eaten for two days and one night. Treating every animal as a possible פסח would cut short the time for eating שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the reason is that he reduces the time for eating שלמים. A פסח is eaten for one day and one night, but שלמים are eaten for two days and one night.
steps.whatsHappening: The shared-כהן suggestion in step 4 solved the חזה ושוק problem, so the גמרא gives a different reason why the conditional offering cannot work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since nobody knows which animal is the real פסח, everyone must follow the stricter פסח rules and burn the leftovers after the first night. But an animal that is really שלמים could still have been eaten for another day. Shortening the time a קרבן may be eaten is not allowed, so the condition fails.

keyTerms.meaning: reduces, shortens
the eating of peace-offerings
for one day and one night (the eating time of a פסח)
for two days and one night (the eating time of שלמים)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the problem is that the meat is lost entirely. The problem is that the time allowed for eating real שלמים gets cut short, because everyone has to burn the leftovers on the פסח schedule.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because he reduces
the eating time of peace-offerings,
for a Paschal lamb is eaten for a day and a night,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִילּוּ שְׁלָמִים לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים וְלַיְלָה אֶחָד.
phrases.english: whereas peace-offerings are eaten for two days and one night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא מְמַעֵיט בַּאֲכִילַת שְׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the חזה ושוק reason, which step 4 knocked down, with a new reason based on eating time.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason (אלא) replacing the rejected one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The condition failed only because of who gets the חזה ושוק, and that problem can be solved by registering a כהן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The condition fails anyway, because it would shorten the eating time of any animal that is really שלמים.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that you may not reduce the time a קרבן may be eaten is why the next suggestion, the מותר הפסח in Step 6, is designed to have the same short eating time as a פסח.

steps.title: Suggestion: use a מותר הפסח, which has the same eating time as a פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that each person stipulate: if my original animal was the one with the מום, this new animal is a פסח; if mine was unblemished, this new animal is a מותר הפסח. A מותר הפסח counts as שלמים but is eaten for only one day and one night, so the eating-time problem disappears.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them bring a מותר הפסח, and each one should say: 'If mine was the blemished one, this animal I am bringing now is a פסח. If mine was unblemished, this animal I am bringing now is שלמים (a מותר הפסח).' A מותר הפסח is eaten for only one day and one night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 5 by suggesting a different kind of condition that gets around the eating-time problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said the condition fails because שלמים get two days while a פסח gets only one. A מותר הפסח counts as שלמים but has the same short eating time as a פסח. So if each person's backup option is a מותר הפסח, nothing gets shortened, and the condition should work.

keyTerms.meaning: a leftover פסח animal that is offered as a kind of שלמים
if mine was the blemished one
unblemished, whole
let it be
is eaten

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word שלמים in the condition means the special kind of שלמים called מותר הפסח, not ordinary שלמים. That is the whole point: this kind has the short, one-day eating time.

phrases.english: But let them bring a surplus Paschal lamb.
And let him say: If mine was the blemished one —
this one that I am bringing now shall be a Paschal lamb;
if mine was unblemished —
this one that I am bringing now shall be a peace-offering,
for a surplus Paschal lamb is eaten
for a day and one night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 5 by proposing a backup option that has the same eating time as a פסח.
steps.kashyaTarget: The eating-time reason given in step 5
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מותר הפסח is a kind of שלמים whose eating time matches a פסח, so making it the backup option means nothing is shortened.

steps.title: You cannot set aside an animal as a מותר הפסח from the start
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. An animal only becomes a מותר הפסח when it was first set aside as a פסח and then was not used. You cannot set aside a fresh animal as a מותר הפסח from the beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: But do we set aside an animal as a leftover from the start?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the מותר הפסח idea from step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By definition, a מותר הפסח is something left over: a פסח animal that ended up unused. A new animal set aside today was never a פסח, so it cannot be called a leftover. Without that status, the backup option would be ordinary שלמים, and the eating-time problem from step 5 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: we set aside (an animal as a קרבן)
from the start, at first
leftovers, surplus animals

phrases.english: But do we designate animals initially as surplus offerings?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6's suggestion by showing that a newly set-aside animal cannot have the status of מותר הפסח.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the idea of creating a new מותר הפסח, not the use of a מותר הפסח in general
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Step 6 assumed you can set aside an animal as a מותר הפסח from the start, but that status comes only from an unused פסח.

steps.title: Then let them find an animal that is already a מותר הפסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers back: fine, so let them go to the trouble of finding an animal that is already a מותר הפסח, meaning a leftover פסח that was never used, and make the condition on that animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let them go to the trouble and bring an animal that is already a מותר הפסח!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the מותר הפסח idea back by suggesting the five people find an animal that already has this status. This sets up the next answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 only showed that you cannot create a new מותר הפסח. It did not rule out using one that already exists. If such an animal is available, the condition from step 6 should work, so the question of why the five people cannot do this is open again.

keyTerms.meaning: and let them go to the trouble
and let them bring

steps.confusionAlert: This line repeats the words of step 6, 'let them bring a מותר הפסח', but now it means something different: find an animal that is already a leftover פסח, not set aside a new one.

phrases.english: So let them trouble themselves and bring a surplus Paschal lamb!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gets around step 7's objection by using an animal that already has the status of מותר הפסח, which brings back the challenge of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the five people have no way to fix their problem with a condition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Step 7 blocks only creating a new מותר הפסח. Finding one that already exists avoids that objection, so the condition from step 6 should still work.

steps.title: The condition fails because of leaning hands on the animal
steps.stepSummary: Even with a real מותר הפסח, the condition cannot work, because a מותר הפסח needs סמיכה and a פסח does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the reason is leaning hands. A פסח does not need leaning hands, but a מותר הפסח does need leaning hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the suggestion from Step 8. It gives a new reason why the condition fails even on a real מותר הפסח: the rules of סמיכה are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מותר הפסח counts as שלמים, so the owner must lean his hands on it. A פסח has no סמיכה. If nobody knows which kind the animal is, nobody knows whether to lean on it, and leaning on an animal that does not need it is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaning one's hands with force on the head of a קרבן before it is slaughtered
Short for מותר הפסח: a leftover פסח that is brought as שלמים
Whereas this one ... while that one (a formula that sets up a contrast)
Does not need

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the problem is only that the owner would skip a מצוה. The problem goes both ways: leaning when it is not needed is also wrong, so the doubt cannot be fixed by simply doing סמיכה just in case.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because of leaning hands.
phrases.notes: אלא signals that a new reason replaces the earlier ones.

phrases.english: For a Paschal offering does not need leaning hands,
whereas a leftover Paschal offering does need leaning hands.
phrases.notes: A מותר הפסח is a type of שלמים, so it needs סמיכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the Step 8 suggestion by finding a new difference between a פסח and a מותר הפסח.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New distinguishing factor (a difference in service)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Using a real מותר הפסח removes every difference, so the condition should work.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is still a difference in סמיכה, so the doubt cannot be handled.

steps.title: Leaning hands does not explain the case of women's offerings
steps.stepSummary: The סמיכה reason only works for men's offerings. Women never do סמיכה, so for them the condition should still work.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for an offering of men. But for an offering of women, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the סמיכה answer from Step 9. It shows that this answer does not cover every case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Women do not do סמיכה on any קרבן. So if the people in the case were women, a פסח and a מותר הפסח would be handled the same way, and the condition should succeed. The reason from Step 9 is therefore too narrow.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out fine (for one case, but not for another)
An offering brought by women
What is there to say? (the explanation does not work here)

phrases.english: This works out well for an offering of men.
phrases.notes: Men's שלמים need סמיכה.

phrases.english: But for an offering of women, what is there to say?
phrases.notes: Women do not do סמיכה, so the difference disappears.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the סמיכה reason given in Step 9.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason does not apply to women's offerings, where no סמיכה is done, so it cannot be the full reason the condition fails.

steps.title: The condition fails because of the number of blood placements
steps.stepSummary: A פסח gets one placement of blood on the מזבח, while שלמים get two placements that count as four. This difference applies to men and women alike.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the reason is the blood placements. A פסח gets one placement, while שלמים get two placements that count as four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the סמיכה reason and gives a new difference that applies to everyone: how the blood is put on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood of a פסח is placed on the מזבח one time. The blood of שלמים, which includes a מותר הפסח, is placed on two opposite corners so that it reaches all four sides. This difference is about the blood, not the owner, so it covers women's offerings too.

keyTerms.meaning: Placements of blood on the מזבח
One placement of blood
Two placements that count as four: blood on two opposite corners that reaches all four sides
Peace offerings

phrases.english: Rather, it is because of the blood placements.
For a Paschal offering gets one placement,
whereas peace offerings get two placements that count as four.
phrases.notes: The blood goes on two opposite corners and so reaches all four sides of the מזבח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the סמיכה reason, which failed in Step 10, with a difference that applies to every owner.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New distinguishing factor that applies to every case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once סמיכה fails for women, maybe no real difference is left.
steps.terutzMaskana: The number of blood placements is different for every owner, so the condition still cannot work.

steps.title: One blood placement already brings atonement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what difference the number of placements makes, since a משנה teaches that one placement on the outer מזבח already brings כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make? Did we not learn in a משנה: all offerings whose blood is placed on the outer מזבח, if one placed it with one placement, the offering has atoned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the blood-placement answer from Step 11. It brings a משנה to show that this difference may not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one placement already makes any outer-מזבח offering valid after the fact, the כהן could simply do one placement. That works whether the animal is a פסח or שלמים, so the difference in placements should not stop the condition.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?
But did we not learn in a משנה?
The outer altar in the courtyard, where most offerings' blood is placed
It has atoned, meaning the offering is valid

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say one placement is the right way to do שלמים from the start. It says that after the fact, one placement is enough for the offering to count.

phrases.english: What difference does it make?
But did we not learn in a mishna:
All offerings whose blood is placed on the outer altar
if one placed it with one placement, it has atoned,
phrases.notes: The quote ends here. The גמרא accepts the challenge, and Step 13 gives a new reason.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the blood-placement reason given in Step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה rules that one placement brings כפרה for any outer-מזבח offering. So the כהן can do one placement, and the doubt between a פסח and שלמים causes no problem.

steps.title: The real difference: pouring versus throwing the blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the 'one placement versus two' answer. It gives a new reason the condition cannot work: a פסח's blood is poured, but שלמים blood is thrown.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the reason is this: a פסח's blood is placed by pouring, while שלמים blood is placed by throwing.
steps.whatsHappening: The question in step 12 knocked out the 'number of placements' reason. So the גמרא now offers a different difference between פסח and שלמים: how the blood is put on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא tells us the previous answer is being replaced. A פסח's blood is gently poured (שפיכה) onto the base of the מזבח. שלמים blood is thrown (זריקה) from the כלי at the מזבח. One action cannot do both jobs, so a condition covering both offerings would leave the כהן not knowing how to place the blood.

keyTerms.meaning: rather; the previous answer is dropped and a new one is given
pouring the blood gently onto the base of the מזבח, as done with a פסח
throwing the blood from the vessel onto the מזבח, as done with שלמים
peace-offerings

phrases.english: Rather, it is because the פסח is done by pouring,
phrases.notes: אלא replaces the 'placements' answer from step 11.

phrases.english: whereas שלמים are done by throwing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge in step 12 by giving up the placements reason and offering a new difference.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacement reason: a new distinction between the two offerings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The condition fails because of the number of blood placements.
steps.terutzMaskana: The condition fails because the method of placing the blood is different: pouring versus throwing.

steps.title: A ברייתא says pouring works even where throwing is required
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new reason. A ברייתא teaches that if blood meant to be thrown was poured instead, the offering is still valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does that make? Wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: any offering whose blood is placed by throwing, if one placed it by pouring, he has fulfilled his obligation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the pouring-versus-throwing answer. It brings a ברייתא showing that pouring also works for offerings that normally need throwing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If pouring is valid even for שלמים, the כהן could simply pour the blood. That pouring would be correct if the animal is a פסח, and still valid if it is שלמים. So the difference in method should not stop the condition from working.

keyTerms.meaning: what practical difference does it make?
but wasn't it taught in a ברייתא? (introduces a contradicting source)
those offerings whose blood is placed in a given way
he has fulfilled his obligation; the offering is valid

phrases.english: What difference does it make?
But wasn't it taught: all offerings that are placed by throwing,
if one placed them by pouring, he has fulfilled his obligation.
phrases.notes: So pouring could serve both possibilities.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the pouring-versus-throwing distinction given in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the difference in how the blood is placed blocks the condition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says pouring is valid even for throwing-offerings. So one pouring would work for either offering, and the difference should not matter.

steps.title: Valid after the fact is not the same as allowed from the start
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא only says pouring works after it was already done. One may not plan to pour שלמים blood לכתחילה, so the condition still cannot be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that we only said it works if he already did it. Did we say he may do so from the start too?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the pouring-versus-throwing answer. The ברייתא only covers a case where the pouring already happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a big difference between בדיעבד, meaning valid once done, and לכתחילה, meaning allowed to plan from the start. A condition would force the כהן to pour possible-שלמים blood on purpose, and that is not allowed. So the condition is rejected, and the whole search for a conditional solution, which began on the previous amud, is closed.

keyTerms.meaning: say; offers a way to limit the source
if he already did it (בדיעבד, after the fact)
from the outset; as a planned, proper practice

steps.whatToRemember: A פסח cannot be brought with a 'if פסח then פסח, if not then שלמים' condition. The two offerings need different handling, and pouring שלמים blood is only valid after the fact, never as a plan.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the ברייתא as saying pouring and throwing are interchangeable. It only says pouring does not ruin the offering once it happened. You still may not choose to do it.
steps.whyThisMatters: The difference between בדיעבד and לכתחילה is a basic tool all over ש״ס. A condition-based plan is rejected if it forces you to rely on a בדיעבד rule from the start.

phrases.english: Say that we said this only if he already did it;
did we say it is allowed from the outset too?!
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question: certainly not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by limiting the ברייתא to after-the-fact cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source: the ברייתא applies only בדיעבד
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since pouring works for throwing-offerings, one could plan to pour and cover both possibilities.
steps.terutzMaskana: Pouring is only valid after the fact. One may not plan it, so the condition remains unusable.

steps.title: משנה: a father slaughters the פסח for whichever son arrives first
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. A father slaughters his פסח 'for whichever of you reaches ירושלים first.' The first son to enter with his head and most of his body acquires his share, and he also gains shares for his brothers along with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who says to his sons, 'I am slaughtering the פסח for whichever of you goes up to ירושלים first': once the first one has brought in his head and most of his body, he acquires his portion, and he acquires for his brothers together with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא's discussion is finished, and a new משנה begins. It describes a father who links his sons' share in the פסח to who reaches ירושלים first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the moment of slaughter, no one knows which son will arrive first. Once one son enters ירושלים with his head and most of his body, he gets his share. Surprisingly, his brothers also get their shares through him.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה
his head and most of his body; the measure for counting as having entered
he acquired his portion
and he acquires portions for his brothers along with him

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who says to his sons:
I am slaughtering the Paschal lamb

phrases.aramaic: עַל מִי שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה מִכֶּם רִאשׁוֹן לִירוּשָׁלַיִם,
phrases.english: for whoever of you goes up first to Jerusalem,
once the first has brought in his head and most of his body,
he has acquired his portion
and he acquires for his brothers together with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה; it starts a new topic after the condition discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first son to enter ירושלים with his head and most of his body acquires his share in the פסח and also brings his brothers in with him.

steps.title: Does the משנה prove that ברירה works?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה that ברירה is accepted: who was registered on the פסח is only clarified later, yet it counts from the start. This is troubling, because ברירה is an unresolved question.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Learn from this that there is ברירה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out what seems to follow from the משנה. It suggests the משנה holds of ברירה, which sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At slaughter time, it was unknown which son was registered. The משנה seems to say that once one son arrives first, he counts as registered from the start. That is ברירה, meaning later events clarify an earlier status. Since the הלכה of ברירה is not settled, this inference is a problem the גמרא will need to solve.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא; the discussion of the משנה begins
learn from this; an inference drawn from a source
retroactive clarification works; a later event shows what was true from the start

steps.confusionAlert: Although it is phrased as 'learn from this,' this is not a happy proof. It works as a challenge, because the גמרא does not want the משנה to settle the open question of ברירה.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Learn from this that there is retroactive clarification!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a troubling inference from the משנה in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain reading of the משנה, where the first son is registered retroactively
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If registration is only decided by who arrives first, the משנה is assuming ברירה. But ברירה is an unresolved question, so the משנה should not be deciding it.

steps.title: The father only wanted to make his children eager
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the father's condition was not a real legal condition. It was a way to motivate his children to hurry to do the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The father said this only to make them eager to do מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the problem from Step 17. The משנה is not about ברירה at all, because the father just wanted his children to rush to the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was how the father could register 'whoever arrives first' if the winner is only known later. רבי יוחנן says the father had really registered all his children from the very beginning. The race was only encouragement and changed nothing legally, so ברירה never comes up.

keyTerms.meaning: to make them eager or quick
commandments
he said (it)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the first son really gets more of the פסח than his brothers. According to רבי יוחנן, everyone was registered equally from the start. The 'prize' was only a motivating trick.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
He (the father) said it in order to make them eager in מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, כְּדֵי לְזָרְזָן בְּמִצְוֹת קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 17 by reinterpreting the case so that it does not involve ברירה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the case: the condition had no legal effect.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father's condition decided after the fact who was registered, which would mean ברירה is accepted.
steps.terutzMaskana: All the children were registered from the start. The condition was only a motivational device, so the משנה is no proof for ברירה.

steps.title: The משנה's wording proves the brothers were registered from the start
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the winner 'acquires for his brothers with him.' The brothers cannot be added after the שחיטה, so they must have been registered from the beginning. This supports רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה's wording also shows this, because it says 'and he acquires shares for his brothers along with him.' If the father registered them from the start, this makes sense. But if he did not register them from the start, can they be registered after the שחיטה? We learned that people may register or withdraw only until the animal is slaughtered. Learn from this that רבי יוחנן is right.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רבי יוחנן from a detail in the משנה itself. The brothers also get a share, and that is only possible if they were registered before the שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the race really decided who was registered, the brothers who lost could never get a share. That is because another משנה says no one can join a פסח after it is slaughtered. Since the משנה says the brothers do share in it, they must have been registered from the start. This is exactly what רבי יוחנן said.

keyTerms.meaning: the wording is also precise (it supports this)
and he acquires for his brothers with him
he registered them
from the beginning
learn from it (proof accepted)

phrases.english: The wording is also precise, for it teaches:
'and he acquires (shares) for his brothers with him.'
Granted, if you say
that he registered them from the beginning, it works well.
But if you say
that he did not register them from the beginning,
can they be registered after he slaughtered it?
But we learned (in a משנה):
People may register and withdraw their hands from it
until it is slaughtered.
Learn from it (that רבי יוחנן is correct).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's answer in Step 18 with a precise reading of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that all the children were registered from the start.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's phrase 'ומזכה אחיו עמו,' combined with the משנה that registration ends at the שחיטה.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the daughters won the race
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells of a real case where the daughters arrived before the sons. This showed the daughters were eager and the sons were lazy, so the race was about eagerness.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: There was a case where the daughters arrived before the sons. The daughters turned out to be eager, and the sons turned out to be lazy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second support for רבי יוחנן from a ברייתא. The story's lesson is about who was eager, not about who legally owned the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sums up the story as a test of eagerness: the daughters were quick and the sons were slow. This fits רבי יוחנן's point that the father's goal was to encourage zeal for the מצוה. The ownership of the קרבן was already settled.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא also teaches this
a real incident
eager, quick (feminine)
lazy, sluggish

steps.whatToRemember: The father's 'whoever arrives first' condition is not a case of ברירה. All the children were registered from the start, and the race was only to make them eager for מצוות. The proofs are the משנה's wording and the ברייתא about the daughters.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא):
There was an incident, and the daughters arrived before the sons,
and it turned out that the daughters were eager
and the sons were lazy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second support, from a ברייתא, for רבי יוחנן's explanation.
steps.raayaObject: That the father's condition was meant only to encourage eagerness.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about daughters who arrived before sons and were praised as eager.

steps.title: New משנה: when people may join or leave a פסח
steps.stepSummary: People may keep joining a פסח as long as each one gets at least a כזית. People may register or withdraw until the שחיטה. רבי שמעון says until the blood is thrown.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: People may always keep registering on a פסח, as long as there is a כזית of meat for each and every person. People may register and withdraw from it until it is slaughtered. רבי שמעון says: until the blood is thrown.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets two limits: a quantity limit (each person needs a כזית) and a time limit (the שחיטה, or according to רבי שמעון the זריקת הדם).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first rule means a group can keep adding members, but only while each member can still get a כזית. The second rule says the list of owners closes at the שחיטה, which is the משנה Step 19 relied on. רבי שמעון holds the list stays open until the blood is thrown on the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: they are registered (join the group of a קרבן פסח)
an olive-sized amount, the minimum to eat
they withdraw their hands (leave the group)
that it is slaughtered
that the blood is thrown on the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה states the rule Step 19 used as its proof: no one can join a פסח after the שחיטה. It also opens the next discussion about the dispute of רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
People may always register on it (the פסח)
as long as there will be in it an olive-sized portion
for each and every one.
People may register and withdraw their hands from it
until it is slaughtered.
Rabbi Shimon says:
Until the blood is thrown.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ לְעוֹלָם נִמְנִין עָלָיו עַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בּוֹ כְּזַיִת לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. Its second rule is the one quoted in Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People may join a פסח as long as each one has a כזית. People may register or withdraw until the שחיטה, and according to רבי שמעון until the זריקת הדם.

steps.title: What is the משנה's first rule teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what new point the משנה's rule about joining a פסח adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the משנה teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks what new thing the משנה's rule about people joining a פסח teaches. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It seems obvious that more people may join a פסח as long as there is enough meat for each one. So the גמרא wants to know what חידוש the משנה is really adding.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion on the משנה
What is it teaching us? (asking for the new point)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of the גמרא's discussion.

phrases.english: What is it teaching us?
phrases.notes: It seems obvious that more people can join.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the משנה rule quoted in step 21 adds.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new point the rule about joining a פסח teaches, since it seems obvious.

steps.title: A whole new group can replace the original group
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that even after one group registered, that group can leave and a completely different group can register on the same animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it teaches us: even though this group was registered on it, the group can withdraw, and a different group can register on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The משנה's point is that one whole group can be swapped out for a new group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might have thought that a פסח stays tied to the people it was first set aside for, so at least one of them must remain. The משנה teaches that this is not needed. Even if every original member leaves, a new group can take over the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: A group registered to eat one קרבן פסח together
They register (are counted) on the פסח
Goes back, here meaning the first group withdraws

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּאִימְּנִי עָלָיו חֲבוּרָה זוֹ,
phrases.english: that even though this group was registered on it,
it can withdraw, and a different group can register on it.
phrases.notes: No one from the original group has to remain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חידוש is that an entire group can be replaced by a new group on the same פסח.

steps.title: אביי: the dispute is only about withdrawing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about registering and withdrawing until the שחיטה. אביי says רבי שמעון disagrees only about withdrawing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'They may register and withdraw their hands until it is slaughtered, etc.' אביי said: The argument is only about withdrawing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. Then אביי explains what the חכמים and רבי שמעון actually argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the משנה alone, it might seem that רבי שמעון lets people both register and withdraw until the blood is thrown. אביי limits the argument to withdrawing only. The next steps explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: They pull back their hands, meaning they withdraw from the פסח
That it is slaughtered (the שחיטה)
A disagreement
To withdraw

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume רבי שמעון allows new people to register after the שחיטה. According to אביי, he only extends the time for leaving.

phrases.english: They may register and withdraw their hands
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: until it is slaughtered, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to רבי שמעון: until the blood is thrown.

phrases.english: Abaye said: The dispute is about withdrawing,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה line from step 21 and defines the scope of its dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument between the חכמים and רבי שמעון is only about the deadline for withdrawing.

steps.title: How each side reads 'from being a lamb'
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים read 'מהיות משה' as 'while the lamb is alive.' רבי שמעון reads it as 'while the lamb's service is still happening.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים hold: 'מהיות משה' means 'from the life of the lamb.' רבי שמעון holds: it means 'from the happenings of the lamb.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the source for each side about withdrawing. Both sides use the same words of the פסוק but read them differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'מהיות משה' is read as permission to withdraw from a lamb. The חכמים connect 'מהיות' to חיות (life), so withdrawing ends at the שחיטה. רבי שמעון connects it to הוויה (happening), so withdrawing is allowed until the service ends with זריקת הדם.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From being from a lamb' (שמות יב:ד), read as withdrawing from a lamb
While the lamb is alive
While the lamb's service is still happening
The חכמים, the majority view

phrases.english: For the Rabbis hold: 'from being from a lamb'
means during the life of the lamb.
phrases.notes: So one can withdraw only until the slaughter.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon holds: during the 'happenings' of the lamb.
phrases.notes: So one can withdraw until the blood is thrown.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's statement by giving the פסוק behind each side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים allow withdrawing until the שחיטה (the lamb's life). רבי שמעון allows it until זריקת הדם (the end of its service).

steps.title: Everyone agrees: registering ends at the slaughter
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees that registering is allowed only until the שחיטה, because the פסוק mentions 'במכסת' (counting) before 'תכסו' (slaughtering).
steps.simpleTranslation: But for registering, all agree it is only until the slaughter, because the פסוק says 'במכסת נפשות' and only afterward 'תכסו'.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his explanation. Both sides agree about the deadline for joining, and he shows the source in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'תכסו' is read as 'you shall slaughter,' like the Aramaic for slaughtering. The פסוק first mentions counting the people ('במכסת') and then slaughtering ('תכסו'). So the counting must come before the שחיטה, and no one can join afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: To register on the פסח
Everyone agrees
'According to the number of people' (the counting)
Read here as 'you shall slaughter'

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי: registering ends at the שחיטה for everyone. Withdrawing ends at the שחיטה for the חכמים, and at זריקת הדם for רבי שמעון.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the time for joining is shorter than the time for leaving: the פסוק itself places the counting before the שחיטה.

phrases.english: But as for registering —
all agree it is only until it is slaughtered,
for the verse says: 'according to the number of the people,'
and only then: 'you shall slaughter (takhosu).'
phrases.notes: Counting comes first, then slaughtering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל לִימָּנוֹת דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל עַד שֶׁיִּשָּׁחֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's statement by showing what both sides agree on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Registering on a פסח is allowed only until the שחיטה, according to everyone.

steps.title: A ברייתא confirms אביי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states clearly that רבי שמעון allows registering only until the שחיטה, and withdrawing until the blood is thrown.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: They may register and withdraw until it is slaughtered. רבי שמעון says: They may register until it is slaughtered, and withdraw until the blood is thrown.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports אביי's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי שמעון himself separates the two deadlines. Registering ends at the שחיטה, and only withdrawing goes until זריקת הדם. This is exactly what אביי said.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא (a supporting source)
That the blood is thrown on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא proves אביי right: רבי שמעון disagrees only about withdrawing, not about registering.

phrases.english: It was also taught so (in a baraita):
They may register and withdraw their hands from it
until it is slaughtered.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: נִמְנִין עַד שֶׁיִּשָּׁחֵט,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: They may register until it is slaughtered,
and withdraw until the blood is thrown.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's explanation from steps 24 through 26.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that the dispute is only about withdrawing
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי שמעון gives separate deadlines: registering until the שחיטה, withdrawing until זריקת הדם
